source_topic: Kelly fraction for a binary bet

follow_up.question: Why is maximising expected log growth different from maximising expected wealth after one round?
follow_up.reference: The objectives weight downside differently. Expected wealth is linear in the stake in this binary model; logarithmic utility penalises near-total losses and produces an interior fraction when the parameters permit it.

instances.text: In an independent repeated betting game, a round wins with probability 14/15. You stake the same fraction f of current wealth each round. A win multiplies wealth by 1+4f; a loss multiplies it by 1-f. What f in [0,1) maximises expected log growth per round?

instances.spoken_text: In a repeated bankroll puzzle, a round wins with probability five over six. You stake the same fraction f of current wealth each round. A win multiplies wealth by one plus twof; a loss multiplies it by one-f. What f in [zero,one, maximises expected log growth per round?

follow_up.question: Why is maximising expected log growth different from maximising expected wealth after one round?
follow_up.reference: The objectives weight downside differently. Expected wealth is linear in the stake in this binary model; logarithmic utility penalises near-total losses and produces an interior fraction when the parameters permit it.

follow_up.reference: The objectives weight downside differently. Expected wealth is linear in the stake in this binary model; logarithmic utility penalises near-total losses and produces an interior fraction when the parameters permit it.
